title: Music everywhere in New Orleans; father's barbershop quartet
summary: Interviewer asks whether the father's barbershop quartet was cutting-edge; Fleming says music was an everyday thing in New Orleans.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Was your father like a real sharp guy? I mean, was this considered, like this barbershop quartet? Was it pretty, you know, hot stuff for that particular period? You know, did they think of it as, you know, kind of being on the, you know, the leading edge of music? Did they think it was pretty exciting to be doing? Was it?

Well, I think it was exciting to them in a way, but it was sort of common in New Orleans because people were singing and playing music or played piano, and so music was just another thing around. Yeah, right. Nobody really thought that this was great or that was great because it was every day, practically something was going on.
And so you were just surrounding my music all the time.
